gloss: rather small; on the small side; smallish

definitions.gloss: rather small; on the small side; smallish
definitions.explanation: Slightly smaller than average or expected, without being extremely small.

examples.japanese: {小|ちい}さめのサイズをください。
examples.english: Please give me the smaller size.

examples.japanese: このシャツは{小|ちい}さめに{作|つく}られている。
examples.english: This shirt is made on the small side.

examples.japanese: {荷物|にもつ}が{多|おお}いので、{小|ちい}さめのバッグでは{入|はい}りきらないかもしれない。
examples.english: Since I have a lot of luggage, a smallish bag might not fit everything.

notes:
Formed by adding the suffix ～め to the adjective stem {小|ちい}さ. The ～め suffix indicates "somewhat" or "leaning toward" a quality, softening the adjective. This is a productive pattern in Japanese that works with many adjectives.

USAGE:
- Modifies nouns with の: {小|ちい}さめの + noun
- Can also be used adverbially with に: {小|ちい}さめに{切|き}る (to cut somewhat small)
- Very common in shopping, cooking, and describing physical dimensions
- The ～め pattern works with other adjectives too: {大|おお}きめ (on the large side), {長|なが}め (on the long side), {早|はや}め (on the early side)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {小|ちい}さめのサイズ: a smaller size
- {小|ちい}さめに{切|き}る: to cut rather small
- {小|ちい}さめの{部屋|へや}: a smallish room
- {少|すこ}し{小|ちい}さめ: a little on the small side

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {小|ちい}さい: small — the base adjective; states the size directly without hedging
- やや{小|ちい}さい: slightly small — similar meaning expressed with an adverb
- {大|おお}きめ: on the large side — the opposite pattern using {大|おお}きい
- コンパクトな: compact — loanword; implies small but well-designed
